notes.text: Full specification for this build lives in the native-GL knowledgebase (an Obsidian vault) on PR #1128: the user-observable outcomes in 'General Ledger - Truth Conditions' (TC-LEDGER-01..15), the system rules in 'General Ledger - Invariants' (INV-LEDGER-01..22), and the architecture narrative in the 'General Ledger' domain hub. In-scope-now items (TC-LEDGER-01..06 / INV-LEDGER-01..13) read 'Holds'; deferred future-build items (TC-LEDGER-07..15 / INV-LEDGER-14..22) read 'Proposed (deferred)'.

The knowledgebase is a behavioural 'digital twin': Truth Condition -> Invariant -> Scenario -> test -> code, traceable by id (TC-/INV-/SCN-LEDGER-NN). Tests cite the scenario id they prove; code cites the invariant id it satisfies. Reading order is top-down from the domain hub.
Agentic-ledger idea: when a backdated entry is posted, automatically detect which reports are affected and surface the delta.

fef38f90-b82c-4c47-b377-6dcb9b1a3020.exec_summary: The ledger is live in production for Ocean Ionics but its first run is not yet trustworthy enough to file from. A new project, "Close out the ledger's first production run" (Mark, In Progress since 10 Aug), was opened off the 19-day post-go-live reading: 138 ledger events, 49 of which never booked - 9 named failures and 40 stalls - with the failure surface under-reporting by roughly five times. The arithmetic itself held (every booked transaction booked once, every failure committed zero lines), so this is queue and surface work, not a corrupted ledger. Mark cleared seven of those defects in the last 36 hours. In parallel the VAT-return mechanics were settled: the net position books to an ordinary payable/receivable with the Belastingdienst as an ordinary party, so a return is literally a bill being paid, and each period is cleared through a VAT suspense account classified as a general account. What is still undecided is the bigger fork - backfill neno's ledger from Exact and take source-of-truth status from a clean cut-off, or keep filing in Exact - which Mark and Matthew reconvene on Friday 14 August.

decisions.text: The net VAT position books to an ordinary payable/receivable with the Belastingdienst as counterparty, the tax authority modelled as an ordinary party - so a VAT return is literally a bill being paid and reuses the existing matching, settlement and outstanding-balance machinery.

"Supplementary return" is split into two distinct outcomes - supplementing the next regular return versus filing a separate correction return for that period - and the one-account-or-a-pair question for corrections was dropped.

Each VAT period is cleared by a counter-booking that zeroes the VAT ledger accounts and posts the net to a VAT suspense account classified as a general account, not a VAT account. The 5 Aug error came from allocating a transaction directly to the BTW receivable account (1520 range), which is blocked by design.
decisions.source: Granola - Clearing VAT return via VAT suspense account, 11 Aug

decisions.text: Exact's own VAT filing feature - which auto-creates a matchable "fake invoice" payable to the Belastingdienst - is the correct mechanism, but has never been used for Ocean Ionics; Venla and Matthew only found it on 6 Aug. neno needs a bridge to Exact that generates the equivalent matchable entry.

VAT is attributed in full to the period the invoice was issued, even when the underlying expense is recognised across multiple periods (subscriptions spread the expense, never the VAT); non-EU regimes (e.g. South Africa) out of scope for current VAT logic.

Closed periods lock writes by default; unlocking is approval-gated and only for material post-close accruals; insert-only with full audit log.

meetings.title: Clearing VAT return via VAT suspense account
meetings.summary: Matthew, Venla, Andries and Mark traced the 5 Aug error to a transaction allocated directly to the BTW receivable account (1520 range), which is blocked by design. The fix is a counter-booking after each VAT period that zeroes the VAT ledger accounts and posts the net to a VAT suspense account, classified as a general account rather than a VAT account - optionally split in two, one for VAT reported and one for VAT paid, so period-by-period discrepancies show up. Exact's own VAT filing feature, which auto-creates a matchable payable to the Belastingdienst, is the right mechanism but has never been used for Ocean Ionics; Venla and Matthew only discovered it on 6 Aug, so neno needs a bridge to Exact that produces the equivalent entry. A Belastingdienst reconciliation strategy has to be in place before September starts.
